did_you_know.text: Did you know? Uzziah became king over Judah when he was only sixteen years old, after the death of his father, Amaziah.
Did you know? Uzziah reigned in Jerusalem for fifty-two years, and his mother was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
Did you know? At the beginning of his reign, Uzziah sought God during the days of Zechariah. Scripture emphasizes: As long as he sought the Lord, God gave him success.
Did you know? Uzziah fought against the Philistines, broke through the walls of Gath, Jabneh, and Ashdod, and built cities in the territory of Ashdod and among the Philistines.
Did you know? Because of his military victories, the Ammonites became subject to him and brought him tribute. Uzziah's fame reached as far as the border of Egypt.
Did you know? Uzziah also developed the land: he dug many cisterns, raised livestock, and encouraged farming, agriculture, and vineyards in the mountains and on Carmel.
Did you know? Uzziah's army included 2,600 heads of ancestral families, along with a fighting force of 307,500 warriors.
Did you know? Uzziah prepared special devices in Jerusalem, on the towers and at the corners, for shooting arrows and hurling large stones at the enemy.
Did you know? After Uzziah became powerful, his heart grew proud, and he entered the temple to burn incense, even though this duty was reserved for the priests, the descendants of Aaron.
Did you know? Azariah the priest came after Uzziah with eighty courageous priests, and they confronted him about entering the temple and wanting to burn incense.
Did you know? When leprosy appeared on Uzziah's forehead, the priests expelled him from the temple. He himself hurried out because the Lord had afflicted him.
Did you know? Uzziah remained leprous until the day he died and lived in a separate house, while his son Jotham managed the royal palace and governed the people.

Did you know? Uzziah was not buried in the tombs of the kings themselves, but in the burial field belonging to the kings, because they said of him, “He is a leper.” After his death, his son Jotham succeeded him as king.
